short: Standard on silent reading (M04) and CTC decoding (M06); 83% WER on 30 sentences repeated in training, with an undisclosed 4-gram LM and no chance baseline, does not show EEG decoding.
position: The paper changes the use-time action (M04, silent reading of displayed sentences) and applies continuous CTC decoding to it (M06); both are standard, since the authors' earlier papers had already applied CTC to EEG recorded during overt speech and listening, and silent reading falls within the reading and imagined-speech actions the field already uses. The feasibility claim does not hold as stated: 83.34% WER is measured on repeats of 30 training sentences, with a 4-gram LM of unreported corpus (M07, not reported) and no chance or shuffled-label baseline. The repeat protocol itself is lenient: on it, the concurrent decoder of Makin et al. reaches about 3% WER for its example participant, though from intracranial ECoG during overt speech. The paper does not show EEG decoding of unseen silently read sentences.
